coverage: Official legislation, courts, patent offices and first-party Git/GitHub documentation relevant to priority, credit, participation, evidence access and monetary routes.

sources.title: git-commit documentation
supports: A commit records a snapshot and declared author, committer and date metadata.
Author and date metadata can be supplied by the caller.
doesNotSupport: Authenticated civil identity
Qualified legal timestamp
First creation or legal entitlement

sources.title: git-commit-tree documentation
supports: The commit object binds a tree, parent relationship and commit metadata.
GIT_AUTHOR_DATE and GIT_COMMITTER_DATE are caller-controlled inputs.
doesNotSupport: Independent verification of real-world event time
Substantive authorship or inventorship

sources.title: About commit signature verification
supports: A verified GPG, SSH or S/MIME signature can bind a supported signing identity to the signed Git object under GitHub's verification rules.
doesNotSupport: First invention
Truth of substantive claims
Copying by a later actor

sources.title: Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, Articles 41 and 42
supports: An electronic timestamp may not be denied legal effect solely because it is electronic or non-qualified.
A qualified electronic timestamp benefits from a presumption of accurate date and time and integrity of the bound data.
doesNotSupport: Identity of the creator
Public availability
Ownership, inventorship or infringement

sources.title: Zivilprozessordnung, section 286
supports: The court evaluates the complete result of the proceedings and evidence according to free conviction, subject to statutory rules.
doesNotSupport: Automatic conclusive effect of an ordinary Git record

sources.title: Patentgesetz, section 3
supports: State of the art includes knowledge made available to the public before the filing date by written or oral description, use or another method.
doesNotSupport: That a merely private timestamp was publicly accessible
That the publisher is the sole inventor

sources.title: EPO Guidelines for Examination G-IV 7.5, Internet disclosures
supports: Internet disclosures can form prior art when public availability and the relevant date are established.
Content, date and actual public accessibility require source-bound assessment.
doesNotSupport: A general patent grace period
Inventorship or ownership from publication alone

sources.title: Patentgesetz, sections 6 to 8, 35, 37, 63, 139 and 140c
supports: The right to the patent belongs to the inventor or successor; joint inventors are jointly entitled.
A filing date, applicant position, inventor designation, entitlement-transfer route, remedies and inspection are distinct legal objects.
doesNotSupport: Patent grant or validity from filing alone
Truth of inventor designation merely because it was filed

sources.title: Urheberrechtsgesetz, sections 2, 7, 8, 10, 13, 31 and 97
supports: Copyright protects personal intellectual creations; the author is the creator.
Joint authorship, attribution, licence scope and infringement remedies have separate statutory conditions.
doesNotSupport: Exclusive control over every abstract idea
A payment claim from resemblance alone

sources.title: Urheberrechtsgesetz, section 69a
supports: Computer-program expression is protected when it is the author's own intellectual creation.
Ideas and principles underlying a program or interface are not protected by program copyright.
Sections 32 to 32g do not apply to computer programs under section 69a(5).
doesNotSupport: Infringement from functional similarity alone
Application of sections 32 to 32g to computer programs

sources.title: Urheberrechtsgesetz, section 69b
supports: Where an employee creates a computer program in execution of duties or according to employer instructions, the employer alone is entitled to exercise all economic rights in the program unless otherwise agreed.
doesNotSupport: Coverage of programs created outside the statutory employment nexus
Authorship, infringement or a payment amount from employment status alone

sources.authority: Court of Justice of the European Union
sources.title: Judgment of 2 May 2012, SAS Institute Inc. v World Programming Ltd, C-406/10
supports: Program functionality, programming language and data-file formats are not forms of program expression protected by software copyright.
Source and object code are protected forms of expression.
doesNotSupport: A licence to copy protected source code
A conclusion that similar output proves derivation

sources.title: Urheberrechtsgesetz, section 101a
supports: Where infringement is sufficiently probable, production and inspection may be available under proportionality and confidentiality safeguards.
doesNotSupport: Automatic infringement finding
Unlimited disclosure of an opponent's records

sources.title: Gesetz zum Schutz von Geschäftsgeheimnissen, sections 2 to 5, 10, 13 and 16
supports: Trade-secret protection requires secrecy, commercial value because of secrecy, reasonable secrecy measures and a legitimate interest in keeping the information secret.
Independent creation and defined reverse engineering can be lawful; unauthorized acquisition, use or disclosure can trigger remedies.

Section 5 permits acquisition, use or disclosure in specified public-interest situations, including freedom of expression and information, disclosure of misconduct in the general public interest, and protection of a legitimate interest.
Litigation can use confidentiality measures.
doesNotSupport: Trade-secret status for information generally known or readily accessible
A claim from public similarity alone

sources.title: Bürgerliches Gesetzbuch, section 812
supports: Restitution requires that the defendant obtained something through performance or otherwise at the claimant's expense and without legal ground.
doesNotSupport: A universal value-participation claim
A claim amount from resemblance or usefulness alone

sources.title: Judgment of 24 March 2016, IX ZR 259/13
supports: Intervention restitution requires a protected position allocated to the right holder for exclusive disposition and exploitation and a benefit contrary to that allocation.
A mere impairment of an exploitation opportunity is insufficient.
doesNotSupport: Restitution for every lost commercial opportunity
A generic ownership right in an unprotected idea

sources.title: Gesetz über Arbeitnehmererfindungen, sections 5 to 9, 12, 31 and 37
supports: A service-invention report, employer claim, transfer of economic rights, appropriate remuneration, co-inventor shares and the arbitration route are distinct steps.
The employer must assist supplementation of an incomplete invention report and timely specify missing information.
doesNotSupport: Coverage of every idea or every software contribution
A predetermined amount without the statutory valuation inputs

sources.authority: German Patent and Trade Mark Office
sources.title: Arbitration Board under the Employee Inventions Act
supports: The confidential, generally fee-free Board seeks an amicable resolution of employee-invention disputes, especially appropriate remuneration.
doesNotSupport: That every employment dispute belongs before the Board
A guaranteed settlement

sources.title: Zivilprozessordnung, section 138
supports: Parties must make complete and truthful factual declarations and respond to the opposing factual assertions in civil litigation.
doesNotSupport: A universal pre-litigation disclosure duty
Automatic truth from silence

sources.title: Zivilprozessordnung, section 142
supports: A court may order a party or third party to produce documents and other records in its possession to which a party has referred, subject to the statutory conditions.
doesNotSupport: An automatic private right to all internal records
Automatic fault from non-production

sources.title: Arbeitsgerichtsgesetz, section 46
supports: Section 46(2) makes the rules of the Code of Civil Procedure generally applicable to first-instance labor-court proceedings unless the Labor Courts Act provides otherwise.
doesNotSupport: Automatic applicability of every civil-procedure rule without checking Labor Courts Act exceptions
A production order, burden reversal or merits finding in a particular case

sources.title: Directive 2004/48/EC, Articles 6 and 7
supports: A party can rely on reasonably available evidence and specify relevant evidence controlled by the opposing party; courts may order production and evidence-preservation measures with confidentiality safeguards.
doesNotSupport: A merits finding from a report alone
A general reversal of every burden of proof

sources.title: Judgment of 16 September 2020, 10 AZR 56/19
supports: In a labor-court dispute about social-fund contribution liability, secondary substantiation could require the knowledgeable opposing party to give a concrete response where the primarily responsible party lacked knowledge and reasonable means of investigation.
doesNotSupport: Automatic reversal of the ultimate burden of proof
A duty to disclose every potentially useful fact

sources.title: Order of 22 August 2013, 1 BvR 1067/12
supports: Pleading requirements may not be handled so that effective legal protection is made factually impossible where decisive events lie in the opposing sphere.
doesNotSupport: A universal presumption in favour of every claimant
An automatic liability finding
